answer: Consider Capability chain with attenuation at each hop as the gate. With each delegation weaker than the last in place, the pulse an attacker faces is not a puzzle to solve once but a cost paid per identity. Honest agents barely notice the check, because each delegation weaker than the last is something they already have; the signal falls entirely on the farm, which must buy or steal it a hundred times. The attacker pays per clone — new hardware, new credentials, new history — while the basalt for the defender stays flat, a single verification per account.
